election._note: By law no later than 15 August 2029 (Dissolution and Calling of Parliament Act 2022); expected polling day 1 May 2029 — Wikipedia 'Next United Kingdom general election'

dissolution._note: The Dissolution and Calling of Parliament Act 2022 repealed the Fixed-term Parliaments Act 2011 and restored the pre-2011 prerogative: the PM may request dissolution from the Sovereign at a time of their choosing, no lockout. Polling day follows roughly 25 working days later. Wikipedia, 'Dissolution and Calling of Parliament Act 2022'; commonslibrary.parliament.uk.

amendment._note: The UK has no codified, entrenched constitution: Parliament alters constitutional arrangements (the electoral system, the devolution settlements, the Union itself) by ordinary Act, under parliamentary sovereignty. No special majority or second vote is required. UK Parliament, 'Parliamentary sovereignty'.
amendment._permits_system_change_note: The same parliamentary sovereignty that sets the amendment bar at an ordinary Act extends to the form of the state itself -- nothing in the UK's uncodified constitution entrenches the monarchy against Parliament.

formation._note: The largest party forms a government; there is no investiture vote. A no confidence motion carries on a simple majority of members present and voting.

government._pretender_note: Whom data/laws/amendments.json's Restoration Act puts on the throne. Authored per nation because the law is generic and the dynasty is not; a monarchy points this at its own sitting monarch.

fiscal._note: General government, IMF/OECD estimates ~2023-2024, rounded. V1.2a starting policy, derived from France's anchor (see FRA.json): VAT 20% is the UK's own statutory standard rate (Tax Foundation, 'VAT Rates in Europe 2024' -- the UK is included for comparison though outside the EU regime). Income and corporate are France's 20/25 scaled by the UK's OECD Revenue Statistics personal/corporate tax-to-GDP share against France's, landing close to France's own. Spending is France's split scaled by general government expenditure of 44.0% of GDP against France's 57.3% (TheGlobalEconomy.com / OECD Government at a Glance 2025).
